reasons.plausibility: The strain‐ and defect‐mediated mechanism is generally consistent with established understanding of how microstructure affects magnetocaloric behavior, although the quantitative link between nanoscale strain relaxation and magnetocaloric changes remains somewhat uncertain.
reasons.testability: A straightforward, controlled comparison of annealed vs. as-deposited samples under the same low-field cycling conditions, paired with direct microstructural characterization, provides a clear and decisive route to falsify or support the hypothesis.
reasons.usefulness: It offers a concrete, experimentally tractable way to clarify whether strain and defects govern magnetocaloric performance in these low-dimensional geometries, which would guide further materials optimization.
